sentences.en: Over the past few days, Californians have watched as the Carr wildfire has raged through the northern part of the state.
sentences.zh: 过去几天里，加州人眼睁睁看着卡尔山火在州北部肆虐。

sentences.en: The fire started a little more than a week ago.
sentences.zh: 这场大火始于一周多前。

sentences.en: Fueled by dry brush, high temperatures, and strong shifting winds,
sentences.zh: 在干燥灌木丛、高温和强劲多变风向的助推下，

sentences.en: the fire has moved from a national recreation area into the nearby city of Reading.
sentences.zh: 火势已从国家游憩区蔓延至附近的雷丁市。

sentences.en: As of this recording, six people have died, 19 people are reported missing, and thousands have evacuated.
sentences.zh: 截至本期节目录制时，已有6人死亡，19人失踪，数千人撤离。

sentences.en: Wildland fires aren't new in California, but with climate change, our fire seasons are becoming longer,
sentences.zh: 野火在加州并不罕见，但随着气候变化，我们的火灾季节变得越来越长，

sentences.en: and fires are becoming bigger and harder to fight.
sentences.zh: 火势也变得越来越大，越来越难以扑灭。

sentences.en: So for the next two weeks, we're going to look at the issue of wildfire,
sentences.zh: 因此，在接下来的两周里，我们将探讨野火问题，

sentences.en: some design solutions, and just how complicated they can be to implement.
sentences.zh: 研究一些设计解决方案，以及这些方案在实施过程中会有多么复杂。

sentences.en: The Santa Ana winds of Southern California are sometimes called the devil winds.
sentences.zh: 南加州的圣安娜风有时被称为“魔鬼之风”。

sentences.en: They pick up in the late summer and early fall, sweeping down from the mountains and across the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 它们在夏末秋初刮起，从山脉呼啸而下，横扫海岸。

sentences.en: They're hot, dry, and known for creating dangerous fire conditions.
sentences.zh: 它们又热又干，以引发危险的火灾条件而闻名。

sentences.en: In late November of 1980, as the Santa Ana's blew in at up to 90 miles an hour,
sentences.zh: 1980年11月下旬，当圣安娜风以高达每小时90英里的速度吹袭时，

sentences.en: an unknown arsonist lit a fire near Panorama Point in the San Bernardino Mountains.
sentences.zh: 一名身份不明的纵火犯在圣贝纳迪诺山脉的全景角附近点燃了一把火。
这是记者斯蒂芬妮·乔伊斯。

sentences.en: Pushed by the wind, the fire grew and quickly spread down the mountain towards the city of San Bernardino.
sentences.zh: 在风的推动下，火势迅速扩大，顺着山坡向圣贝纳迪诺市蔓延。

sentences.en: This is the city's then-fire chief talking to a reporter.
sentences.zh: 这是当时该市的消防局长在接受记者采访。

sentences.en: Again, we had extremely strong winds.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，当时风力极其强劲。

sentences.en: Another local fire chief said they called in all available resources.
sentences.zh: 另一位当地消防局长说，他们调动了所有可用资源。

sentences.en: There was no stopping the fire.
All the conditions were just right for what we commonly refer to as a firestorm.
sentences.zh: 所有的条件都恰好促成了我们通常所说的“火风暴”。

sentences.en: In just a few hours, the Panorama Fire destroyed hundreds of homes and killed four people.
sentences.zh: 仅仅几个小时内，全景大火就摧毁了数百座房屋，造成4人死亡。

sentences.en: It was one of the worst wildfire disasters in California history at the time.
sentences.zh: 那是当时加州历史上最严重的野火灾难之一。

sentences.en: It was also the fire that would make a young researcher question our entire approach to wildfires
sentences.zh: 也正是这场大火，让一位年轻的研究人员开始质疑我们应对野火的整体方式，

sentences.en: and conclude that we might be able to design our way out of the devastation they cause.
sentences.zh: 并得出结论：我们或许可以通过设计来摆脱野火造成的破坏。

sentences.en: Jack Cohen was a few years out of graduate school and a recent transplant to California at the time of the fire.
sentences.zh: 杰克·科恩在火灾发生时刚从研究生院毕业几年，也是刚搬到加州不久。

sentences.en: He was working as a research scientist for the Forest Service, studying fire behavior.
sentences.zh: 他当时在林务局担任研究科学家，专门研究火灾行为。

sentences.en: And he was interested in how the Panorama Fire had destroyed so many homes,
sentences.zh: 他很想知道全景大火为何摧毁了如此多的房屋，

sentences.en: especially when there was such an overwhelming firefighting response.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在当时有如此大规模消防力量响应的情况下。

sentences.en: A strike team of engines is five engines, and they had 20 strike teams coming in right away.
sentences.zh: 一个消防队由五辆消防车组成，当时他们立刻调集了20个消防队。

sentences.en: There would be a whole block of houses on fire, and they could not deliver enough water.
sentences.zh: 整条街的房子都在燃烧，但他们无法提供足够的水。

sentences.en: So they were calling in more hoses and moving a block down or two blocks down and losing that,
sentences.zh: 所以他们只能呼叫更多的水管，然后转移到下一条街或再下一条街，结果还是守不住，

sentences.en: and then moving further and losing that.
sentences.zh: 接着继续转移，还是守不住。

sentences.en: So Jack started listening to the emergency dispatch tapes from the day of the fire.
sentences.zh: 于是杰克开始听火灾当天的紧急调度录音。

sentences.en: Jack is a matter-of-fact kind of guy, a scientist, rational, not emotional.
sentences.zh: 杰克是个实事求是的人，一名科学家，理性且冷静。

sentences.en: But almost 40 years later, he still chokes up when he talks about the desperation he heard in the firefighters' voices.
sentences.zh: 但近40年后，当他谈起在消防员声音中听到的绝望时，依然会哽咽。

sentences.en: The tapes are pretty hard to understand, but you can hear the emotion.
sentences.zh: 录音很难听清，但你能感受到其中的情绪。

sentences.en: It was pretty emotional, particularly listening to the radio traffic.
sentences.zh: 那确实非常令人揪心，尤其是听无线电通话记录的时候。

sentences.en: Because of how they couldn't fight it.
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本无法扑灭大火。

sentences.en: For those of us who mostly see wildfires on TV, or in pictures in the paper,
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些大多通过电视或报纸图片了解野火的人来说，

sentences.en: it's easy to imagine that a wildfire is like a tsunami of flames,
sentences.zh: 很容易想象野火就像一场火焰海啸，

sentences.en: spreading across the landscape and destroying everything in its path.
sentences.zh: 横扫大地，摧毁沿途的一切。

sentences.en: But Jack knew it wasn't that simple when he set out to piece together how the disaster had unfolded.
sentences.zh: 但杰克在着手拼凑灾难发生过程时，就知道事情没那么简单。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that I did was to look at when the first call came in
sentences.zh: 所以我做的一件事就是查看第一次接到报警电话的时间，

sentences.en: to dispatch for a fire in this community,
sentences.zh: 那是关于社区火灾的调度电话，

sentences.en: where was that call from, and where was the wildfire at that time?
sentences.zh: 那个电话是从哪里打来的，当时野火又在哪里？

sentences.en: And as Jack was listening to the tapes, he started to notice a pattern.
sentences.zh: 当杰克听着录音时，他开始注意到一个规律。

sentences.en: People were calling in about houses on fire long before the fire front ever reached their neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 人们在火线到达他们社区之前很久，就已经在报警说房子着火了。

sentences.en: The wildfire was still actually on the other side of the ridge,
sentences.zh: 当时野火实际上还在山脊的另一侧，

sentences.en: about a half a mile away, burning up the hill.
sentences.zh: 大约半英里外，正顺着山坡向上燃烧。

sentences.en: These houses weren't burning because a wall of fire was racing through the community.
sentences.zh: 这些房子着火并不是因为有一堵火墙冲进了社区。

sentences.en: They were burning because of something else.
sentences.zh: 它们着火是因为别的原因。

sentences.en: As wildfires burn, they generate embers that are lofted downwind ahead of the main body of the fire.
sentences.zh: 野火燃烧时会产生火星，这些火星被风吹向火场主体的前方。

sentences.en: And Jack realized most of the houses that burned had one extremely problematic feature in common.
sentences.zh: 杰克意识到，大多数被烧毁的房屋都有一个极其严重的问题特征。

sentences.en: As it turns out, every house had a flammable wood roof.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，每栋房子都有易燃的木质屋顶。

sentences.en: The embers were accumulating in the crevices around the dry wood shingles
sentences.zh: 火星积聚在干木瓦的缝隙中，

sentences.en: and setting fire to the houses from above.
Across the street, in a development without wood roofs, most of the houses had survived.
sentences.zh: 而在街对面，在一个没有木质屋顶的开发区，大多数房屋都幸存了下来。

sentences.en: And while that might not seem like a huge epiphany,
sentences.zh: 虽然这看起来可能算不上什么惊人的顿悟，

sentences.en: that houses with wood roofs burned and houses without wood roofs didn't,
sentences.zh: 即有木屋顶的房子烧了，没木屋顶的没烧，

sentences.en: for Jack, it was that detail that made him rethink the entire wildfire problem.
sentences.zh: 但对杰克来说，正是这个细节让他重新思考了整个野火问题。

sentences.en: Because when you listen to other people talk about the fire,
sentences.zh: 因为当你听别人谈论这场大火时，

sentences.en: they weren't focusing on the wood roofs.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有关注木质屋顶。
他们谈论的是消防工作。

sentences.en: And they were saying nothing could have been done.
sentences.zh: 他们说当时已经无能为力了。

sentences.en: Like this captain in the San Bernardino Fire Department.
sentences.zh: 就像圣贝纳迪诺消防局的这位队长所说。

sentences.en: If we would have had as many as 500 units spread along the whole hillside there to protect those homes,
sentences.zh: 如果我们当时在整个山坡上部署了多达500个单位来保护那些房屋，

sentences.en: I don't believe that we could have stopped that fire any better than we did under the conditions that we had.
sentences.zh: 在当时那种条件下，我不认为我们能比现在做得更好。

sentences.en: The only thing that I feel is that what could have saved those homes would have only been an act of God.
sentences.zh: 我唯一的感觉是，能拯救那些房屋的只有上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: Jack didn't think that was right.
The problem wasn't the firefighting response.
The problem was that the houses were built to burn.
sentences.zh: 问题在于这些房子本身就是为了燃烧而建造的。

sentences.en: And when Jack shifted his focus from the fire to the design of the homes,
sentences.zh: 当杰克将注意力从火灾本身转移到房屋设计上时，

sentences.en: suddenly he found himself wondering if we were framing the whole problem of wildfire in the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 他突然开始怀疑，我们是否从一开始就用错误的方式看待野火问题。

sentences.en: He wasn't the first to have that thought,
sentences.zh: 他并不是第一个有这种想法的人，

sentences.en: but he was the first to do extensive research into exactly how homes burn in wildfires.
sentences.zh: 但他却是第一个对野火中房屋如何燃烧进行深入研究的人。

sentences.en: Some of that work put him at odds with some of the main firefighting agencies in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这项工作中的一部分让他与美国一些主要的消防机构产生了分歧，

sentences.en: and nearly 100 years of fire policy and tradition.
sentences.zh: 也挑战了近100年的消防政策和传统。

sentences.en: And even though his ideas are simple and compelling,
sentences.zh: 尽管他的观点简单且令人信服，

sentences.en: they still haven't caught on in the way that he hoped they would.
sentences.zh: 但它们至今仍未像他所希望的那样普及开来。

sentences.en: Maybe because fighting fires is as much a social and political problem as it is a technical one.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为扑灭野火既是一个技术问题，也是一个社会和政治问题。

sentences.en: Do you feel frustrated most of the time?
sentences.zh: 你大部分时间都感到沮丧吗？

sentences.en: For most of this country's history,
sentences.zh: 在这个国家历史的大部分时间里，

sentences.en: our approach to wildfire has been driven by the sentiment,
sentences.zh: 我们应对野火的方式一直受一种情绪驱动，

sentences.en: Before colonization, many Native American tribes set fires intentionally
sentences.zh: 在殖民之前，许多美洲原住民部落会故意放火，

sentences.en: to regenerate wild plants and to create grasslands and habitat for game.
sentences.zh: 以促进野生植物再生，并创造草地和猎物栖息地。

sentences.en: But when Europeans arrived, they brought fear of fire with them.
sentences.zh: 但当欧洲人到来时，他们也带来了对火的恐惧。

sentences.en: And over time, in much of the country,
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，在该国大部分地区，

sentences.en: not only did we do away with the practice of setting fires,
sentences.zh: 我们不仅废除了放火的习俗，

sentences.en: we actually started to extinguish naturally occurring fires too.
sentences.zh: 甚至开始扑灭自然发生的火灾。

sentences.en: In 1911, that became an official responsibility of the newly created Forest Service.
sentences.zh: 1911年，这成为了新成立的林务局的一项官方职责。

sentences.en: And in 1935, that policy even got a name, the 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 1935年，这项政策甚至有了个名字，叫“上午10点规则”。
规则规定，林务局应在次日上午10点前扑灭公共土地上的每一场新火灾。

sentences.en: It said the Forest Service should put out every new fire on public land by 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福总统的平民保育团是实施该政策的一线力量。
我们有时没日没夜地扑灭那些火灾。

sentences.en: President Roosevelt's Civilian Conservation Corps was on the front lines of implementing that policy.
sentences.zh: 很多天，特别是在春天，你可以看到烟雾一直蔓延到世界的尽头。

sentences.en: We fought those fires night and day sometimes.
sentences.zh: 当时人们相信，只要有足够的水和人力，

sentences.en: Lots of days, especially in the spring, you could see smokes clear to the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 消防员就能扑灭任何野火。

sentences.en: The belief was that with enough water and manpower,
sentences.zh: 围绕这一理念，一个庞大的产业兴起了。

sentences.en: firefighters could put out any wildfire.
sentences.zh: 它发展到雇佣了数万人，

sentences.en: And a huge industry rose up around that idea.
sentences.zh: 每年花费数亿美元用于飞机、直升机和消防队。

sentences.en: It grew to employ tens of thousands of people,
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，这种蛮力扑灭的方法似乎确实有效。

sentences.en: with hundreds of millions of dollars a year being spent on planes and helicopters and fire crews.
sentences.zh: 但那些早期的消防员有一个优势。

sentences.en: And for a while, that brute force approach seemed to work.
sentences.zh: 在现代灭火技术兴起之前的几千年里，

sentences.en: But those early firefighters had an advantage.
sentences.zh: 野火经常在美国的森林中燃烧。

sentences.en: For millennia, before the rise of modern fire suppression,
sentences.zh: 它们会消耗掉所有的燃料。

sentences.en: wildfires had burned regularly through America's forests.
sentences.zh: 所以当火灾发生时，它们通常强度较低，且只停留在森林地面上。

sentences.en: They would eat up all the fuel.
sentences.zh: 随着消防员开始积极扑灭火灾，这种平衡开始改变。

sentences.en: So when there were fires, they were often low intensity and stayed on the forest floor.
sentences.zh: 由于燃烧的火灾减少，森林开始变得越来越茂密。

sentences.en: As firefighters began aggressively fighting fires, that balance started to change.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当森林真的着火时，

sentences.en: With fewer fires burning, forests started getting more and more dense.
sentences.zh: 有更多的可燃物，火势也会烧得更猛、更大。

sentences.en: That meant when the forest did catch on fire,
sentences.zh: 实际上，通过扑灭自然火灾，

sentences.en: there was more material to burn and the fires burned hotter and bigger.
sentences.zh: 我们制造出了一种结果更糟糕的东西。

sentences.en: we created something that turned out to be much, much worse.
sentences.zh: 他是林务局的一位火灾科学家。
扑灭火灾确实产生了一些意想不到的后果，

sentences.en: He's a fire scientist with the Forest Service.
sentences.zh: 这些后果可能比火灾本身更糟糕，而且往往确实如此。

sentences.en: Fighting fire really has some unintended consequences
sentences.zh: 自从我们的灭火政策实施之初，

sentences.en: that may be even worse than the fire itself, and often are.
sentences.zh: 就一直有人认为扑灭每一场火灾并不是个好主意。

sentences.en: Since the very beginnings of our fire suppression policies,
sentences.zh: 但直到20世纪80年代，这个想法才真正站稳脚跟。

sentences.en: there have been people arguing that it wasn't a good idea to put out every fire.
sentences.zh: 到那时，人们也越来越清楚地认识到，我们无法扑灭每一场火灾，

sentences.en: But it took until the 1980s for that idea to really take hold.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当火势变得越来越大时。

sentences.en: By then, it was also becoming increasingly clear that we couldn't put out every fire,
sentences.zh: 我们实际上并没有阻止它们。

sentences.en: especially as they got bigger and bigger.

sentences.zh: 你知道，有句谚语说，扑灭一场火，就是推迟一场火。
但即使在20世纪80年代，公众开始接受火灾是自然且必要的一部分，

sentences.en: You know, there's the saying, a fire put out is a fire put off.
sentences.zh: 且扑灭它会带来意想不到的后果这一观点时，

sentences.en: But even as the public in the 1980s started to accept the idea that fire was natural and necessary,
sentences.zh: 在偏远的荒野地区之外，不扑灭火灾似乎并不是一个可行的选择。

sentences.en: and fighting it had unintended consequences,
sentences.zh: 因为当火灾威胁到人们的家园时，你怎么能停止灭火呢？

sentences.en: not fighting it didn't seem like a viable option outside of remote wilderness areas.
sentences.zh: 这又把我们带回了全景大火中的杰克·科恩。

sentences.en: Because how could you stop fighting fires when they threatened people's homes?
sentences.zh: 一旦他开始将房屋视为问题所在，而不是野火本身，

sentences.en: Which brings us back to Jack Cohen in the Panorama Fire.
sentences.zh: 他就想知道是什么让一些房屋比其他房屋更容易受灾。

sentences.en: Once he started to focus on the home as the problem, not the wildfire,
sentences.zh: 这是我脑海中产生的一个问题，一个好奇心驱使的问题。

sentences.en: he wanted to know what made some houses more susceptible than others.
sentences.zh: 我试图建立野火与房屋损毁之间的关系。

sentences.en: This was a question that I had in my mind, a curiosity question.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这种联系是什么。

sentences.en: What I'm trying to do is to establish a relationship between wildfire and home destruction.
I want to know what that linkage is.
sentences.zh: 在全景大火中，显然是木质屋顶的问题。
但在其他火灾中，也有许多没有木质屋顶的房屋被烧毁了。

sentences.en: In the Panorama Fire, it had clearly been the wood roofs.
sentences.zh: 所以杰克开始着手了解房屋所有潜在的弱点。

sentences.en: But in other fires, there were plenty of homes without wood roofs that burned too.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他要研究房屋的每一个细节。

sentences.en: So Jack set about learning all of a house's potential weaknesses,
sentences.zh: 他想知道火灾是如何从野外蔓延到家里的。

sentences.en: all the ways it might plausibly catch on fire.
sentences.zh: 所有可能导致起火的方式。

sentences.en: The first thing he wanted to know was how close the flames of a wildfire had to be to a house
sentences.zh: 他首先想知道的是，野火的火焰距离房屋多近

sentences.en: for it to ignite simply from the radiant heat.
sentences.zh: 才会仅凭辐射热就将其点燃。

sentences.en: To answer that question, he did a series of experiments,
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，他进行了一系列实验，

sentences.en: including one in the late 1990s in northern Canada, where he set an actual forest on fire.
sentences.zh: 其中包括 20 世纪 90 年代末在加拿大北部进行的一次实验，他在那里点燃了一片真正的森林。

sentences.en: So you actually like cut plots into a forest?
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上是在森林里开辟了样地？

sentences.en: And then set them on fire?
What Jack found in the experiment was that an entire forest could be on fire,
sentences.zh: 杰克在实验中发现，即使整片森林都在燃烧，
